stem:
Meena's teacher asks the class why conserving microalgae in ponds and lakes matters.
Which reason is correct?

options.text: Microalgae use sunlight to make their own food and help keep the oxygen balance of the environment.
Microalgae supply nitrogen to the air instead of oxygen when they make food using sunlight.
Microalgae can keep making their own food by the same process even in permanent darkness.
Conserving microalgae increases pollution because abundant microalgae cause it.

teacher.key_rationale: A correctly states that microalgae photosynthesise using sunlight and support oxygen balance, which underpins environmental health, food security, and livelihoods. B reverses the gas involved (nitrogen vs oxygen), C omits the need for sunlight, and D reverses the conservation-pollution relationship.
